wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/zlib_incremental_surface.py: """What do zlib's seven remaining functions actually DO, call by call?

They are described as needing incremental compression state, which would put them out of reach of a
PHP prelude. That description is not a measurement. What decides it is what each call RETURNS: if
`deflate_add(..., ZLIB_NO_FLUSH)` answers the empty string and only `ZLIB_FINISH` produces bytes,
then the common pattern is an ACCUMULATOR and a one-shot compress — which the primitives already
here can do exactly. If the intermediate calls emit bytes, they cannot.
